title: Deep phenotyping the right ventricle to establish translational MRI biomarkers for characterization of adaptive and maladaptive states in pulmonary hypertension.
summary: In rat pulmonary-hypertension models, machine-learning analysis linked MRI features to adaptive versus maladaptive right-ventricular states and identified extracellular-matrix increases at insertion points and septum during maladaptation; histopathology and RNA-sequencing results provided corroborating measurements. Proposed markers remain preclinical.
ai_technology: Supervised classification and feature ranking linked MRI measures to adaptive or maladaptive right-ventricular states in pulmonary-hypertension models.
organization: National Heart and Lung Institute, Faculty of Medicine, Imperial College London, UK; Biological Imaging Centre, Imperial College London, UK; Department of Lung Development and Remodeling, Max Planck Institute for Heart and Lung Research, Germany; Department of Internal Medicine, Universities of Giessen and Marburg Lung Center, Justus Liebig University, Germany

evidence.tested: The study reports MRI features associated with adaptive and maladaptive RV states and an extracellular-matrix increase at RV insertion points and septum in maladaptation.
evidence.unknown: Findings were studied in monocrotaline and Sugen-hypoxia rat models; histopathology and RNA sequencing were used as corroborating measurements. Proposed translational markers are not clinically validated.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning analysis connected MRI features with measured pathological states in two rat pulmonary-hypertension models.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods and Results in Europe PMC; publisher publication date checked.
